memory.lesson: checkout-api p99 latency breached threshold with flat CPU: connection pool exhausted, acquire timeouts, waiters queueing. That is pool exhaustion, not compute pressure. Cause was PR #4471 deployed to ledger-service 2 hops upstream, touching src/db/connection-pool.ts. Pooled client reuse in the hot path reduced the effective pool ceiling, so callers queued on acquire and the latency surfaced at the customer-facing service rather than at the service that changed. Fix: raise the pool ceiling and add a per-caller bulkhead. For this signature, check pool saturation before CPU.

incidents.title: ledger-service connection pool exhaustion under checkout retry storm
incidents.symptom: ledger-service p99 latency 6100ms, connection pool exhausted, acquire timeouts, waiters queueing, checkout retries amplifying load
incidents.lesson: ledger-service ran a fixed Postgres pool of 20 connections. A retry storm from checkout-api saturated it and every caller queued on acquire, so p99 latency climbed while CPU stayed flat -- the signature of pool exhaustion rather than compute pressure. Fix was to raise the pool ceiling to 60 and add a per-caller bulkhead in src/db/connection-pool.ts so one noisy upstream cannot consume the whole pool. Check pool saturation before chasing CPU whenever latency rises with flat utilisation.

CALL db.idx.vector.queryNodes('Incident','embedding', $k, vecf32($v))
    YIELD node, score
    WHERE node.status = 'resolved'
    OPTIONAL MATCH (node)-[:PRODUCED]->(pm:Postmortem)
    OPTIONAL MATCH (node)-[:AFFECTED]->(s:Service)
    OPTIONAL MATCH (node)-[:RESOLVED_BY]->(p:Person)
    OPTIONAL MATCH (node)-[:CAUSED_BY]->(d:Deploy)-[:SHIPS]->(pr:PullRequest)
    RETURN node, score, pm, collect(DISTINCT s.name) AS services,
           collect(DISTINCT p.name) AS resolvers, pr.number AS pr_number

events.cypher:
MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKED_ON]->(f:File)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(owner:Service)
    WHERE f.path = $target OR f.path CONTAINS $target OR owner.name = $target
    OPTIONAL MATCH (i:Incident)-[:IMPLICATED]->(f)
    OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[:RESOLVED_BY]->(p)
    OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(t:Team)
    RETURN p, t.name AS team,
           sum(w.commits) AS commits,
           max(w.last_at) AS last_at,
           count(DISTINCT i) AS prior_incidents,
           collect(DISTINCT f.path) AS files,
           collect(DISTINCT owner.name) AS services
    ORDER BY prior_incidents DESC, commits DESC
    LIMIT 8

args.lesson: notifications-api p99 latency rose with flat CPU: connection pool exhausted, acquire timeouts, waiters queueing. Same connection pool exhaustion signature already recorded against ledger-service. Latency climbing while utilisation stays flat means callers are queueing on a pool, not waiting on compute. Applied the known fix: raise the pool ceiling and add a per-caller bulkhead so one upstream cannot consume the whole pool. For this signature, check pool saturation before CPU.

events.cypher:
MATCH (i:Incident {id:$incident})
        MERGE (pm:Postmortem {id:$pm_id})
        SET pm.lesson = $lesson, pm.created_at = $now, pm.created_by = 'blackbox',
            pm.embedding = vecf32($vec),
            pm.cause_pr = $cause_pr, pm.cause_deploy_id = $cause_deploy_id,
            pm.cause_service = $cause_service, pm.cause_file = $cause_file,
            pm.cause_hops = $cause_hops, pm.affected_count = $affected_count,
            pm.customer_facing = $customer_facing
        MERGE (i)-[:PRODUCED]->(pm)
        WITH pm, i
        OPTIONAL MATCH (s:Service {name:$service})
        FOREACH (x IN CASE WHEN s IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [1] END |
                 MERGE (pm)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(s))
        RETURN pm, i.title
